category.description:
Product category the endpoint belongs to. On the `2025-11-01`
version the values are `Company`, `Person`, `Jobs`, `Web`,
`Social`, and `Other`. This is the value the `category`
query parameter matches on, case-insensitively.

status.description:
Whether the endpoint is enabled for this account. An endpoint marked
`disabled` is not callable on the current plan; see that endpoint's
own reference page for the permission error it returns.

effective_rate_limit_rpm.description:
Effective rate limit for this endpoint in requests per minute: the
endpoint-specific limit when one is configured, otherwise the
account default. Values observed on the `2025-11-01` version are
5, 10, 15, 30, 45, and 300. It is `null` when no limit applies,
currently only on `/batch/person/identify`.

base_credits.description:
Credits this account is charged per result the endpoint returns.
Absent on endpoints that carry no per-result charge. Every price on
this endpoint is the account's own effective price, so a contract or
grandfathered rate shows here as the rate that account actually pays.

premium_modes.description:
Request flags that change what the call costs, such as `preview` on
live search or `verified` on contact enrich. Absent when the endpoint
has none. See the endpoint's own page for what each flag does.

premium_filters.description:
Fields that cost extra to filter on, charged per result returned.
Sorting on a premium field is free. Absent on endpoints without
premium filtering, which is every endpoint except search.

premium_fields.description:
Fields that cost extra to receive, charged per result that comes
back carrying them. Absent when the endpoint prices no field this
way. A field priced to filter on but never returned appears only in
`premium_filters`.

EnrichMatch.description: A single enriched company match from /company/enrich with confidence score and full company data.

EnrichResult.description: One result entry in the enrich response — one per submitted identifier.

EntityResults.description: Entity payload. One object per subject that fired on this run.

changes.description: Exactly what moved. Reported whatever `fields` says, so a change is always legible even with the default projection.

record.description:
The subject's current data, projected to the watch's `fields`, in the same shape the
dataset's enrich endpoint returns. The subject's identity travels inside the record
as `crustdata_person_id` or `crustdata_company_id`.

EntitySubjects.description:
The records to watch, as a map of identifier type to values. The accepted keys are exactly the
ones the dataset's enrich endpoint accepts, and they are resolved to canonical ids when the
watch runs. One watch holds up to 10,000 subjects across all keys.

People accept `professional_network_profile_urls` and `business_emails`. Companies accept
`domains`, `names`, `professional_network_profile_urls`, and `crustdata_company_ids`. Company
ids must be positive integers; every other identifier is a non-empty string.

professional_network_profile_urls.description: Profile URLs. Valid for both `person` and `company`.

crustdata_company_ids.description: Crustdata company ids, the exact identifier. `company` only.

EntityTestPreviewRequest.description:
An in-progress entity watch config to build a sample from. Carries the same `track` and `fields`
a create request would, but nothing is saved.

track.description: The track tree to build the sample `changes` array from.

fields.description: Field groups to project the sample `record` to. Entitlement-checked like a create.

notification_endpoint.description: Public URL to deliver the sample to. Required when `deliver` is not `false`, since there is no saved watch to fall back on.

deliver.description: Set `false` to get the envelope back without sending anything.

EntityTestRequest.description: Options for an entity watch's test send. Every field is optional.

notification_endpoint.description: Deliver this one test to a public URL you control instead of the watch's configured channels.

fields.description: Project the sample `record` to a chosen field set for this test. Defaults to the watch's own `fields`, and is entitlement-checked like a create.

count.description: Deliver this many sample subjects in one envelope. Each gets a distinct record id.

deliver.description: Set `false` to build and return the envelope without sending anything.

EntityWatch.description: An entity watch, as returned by create, get, list, and update.

EntityWatchConfig.description: Schedule, per-run caps, and data freshness for an entity watch.

max_results_per_run.description:
Most notifications to deliver in one run.

A value above 1000 requires `config.payload_delivery_type` of `link`, on create and on
PATCH. Inline delivery stops at 1000 records per run.

refresh_frequency_days.description:
How fresh the tracked data is kept, in days. This is independent of
`trigger.every_hours`: `every_hours` is how often the watch checks and notifies, while
this is how up to date the data it checks against is, which is what decides how quickly
a real change is detected.

Fresher data costs more per notification: 5 credits at 30 days (the default), 10 at 14,
20 at 7, 50 at 3, 150 at 1. A value between two tiers is billed at the fresher tier.
Only fields backed by a refresh asset can be kept fresh this way, so a tracked field
with no backing asset makes the create fail. Company watches have a higher minimum than
person watches.

preferred_hour.description: Hour of day, in UTC, to prefer for the run.

payload_delivery_type.description:
Where the run's records travel. `inline` puts them in the notification body under
`results`, split across several requests when a run is large. `link` leaves the body
carrying no records at all and adds `metadata.payload_delivery`, a pre-signed S3 URL
for one NDJSON file holding every record of the run.

`link` is required when `config.max_results_per_run` is above 1000, because inline
delivery stops at 1000 records per run.

Switch to `link` when a run can exceed what your receiver accepts: an AWS Lambda proxy
integration caps a request at 6 MB and an ALB target at 1 MB, and an oversize body is
refused whole. `inline` is never overridden by size, so a large run stays inline and
is split instead.

Mutable. Changing it leaves the watch's filters, tracked fields, and sort order
untouched, but a `config` PATCH is validated whole, so send the current `trigger`
alongside it. A create, `GET`, or `PATCH` response echoes the stored value under
`config.payload_delivery_type`, but that is the watch's setting rather than what a
given run did: read `metadata.payload_delivery.type` on a notification, or
`payload_delivery.type` on a run summary, to see which mode a run actually used, since
a `link` watch falls back to `inline` when the file cannot be written.

EntityWatchCreateRequest.description: Body for creating an entity watch. The dataset comes from the path.

preview.description:
Ask what this watch would do instead of creating it. The request is validated exactly as a
create is, nothing is persisted, and no credits are charged or reserved — so a preview works
even on an account with no credits left, which is the balance a preview is usually being run
to inform.

Answers `200` with the preview rather than `201` with a watch. Everything else in the body
means the same thing it means on a create, so preview and create differ by this flag alone.

track.description: The change that fires a notification. A single leaf or a nested AND/OR group.

fields.description:
Field groups to include in each delivered `record`, using the same names and nesting as
the dataset's enrich endpoint. There is no wildcard: list every group you want. Omit it
and the record falls back to a minimal projection, which for a person is
`basic_profile` plus `social_handles`.

The tracked field is not added to the payload automatically. `fields` does not affect
the price, so request whatever your workflow needs, and note that some groups need a
field-level entitlement on your key.

notifications.description:
Delivery channels. The key is required on an entity create, but the list may be empty
for a pull-only watch, which pushes nothing and whose results you read from the
run-history endpoints instead.

EntityWatchPreview.description:
What an entity watch would track, and which of the identifiers you supplied could not be read.
Resolution covers every identifier because it is an id lookup; the sample covers three, because
reading their stored records is the part that costs something.

resolved.description: How many of your identifiers matched a record we hold.

unresolved.description:
The identifiers that matched nothing. Worth reading before arming: an identifier that
matches nothing is invisible afterwards — the watch simply never reports on it.

sample.description:
Up to three of the resolved subjects, cut to identity — a name and a link. This answers
"did you find the people I pasted", not "what do those people look like right now".

tracked_fields.description:
The tracked paths your key is entitled to. A path you sent that is missing here has no
grant behind it and will never fire.

EntityWatchUpdateRequest.description:
Body for updating an entity watch. Only these four keys are accepted. Sending `track`, `fields`,
`dataset`, `kind`, `api_version`, `filters`, `sorts`, or `on` returns `400`.

FieldPrice.description:
What one field costs this account on one side of a request. `field` is a
path prefix: a root such as `experience` covers every path beneath it, and
the longest matching prefix wins, so `dev_platform_profiles.repos` is priced
by its own entry rather than by `dev_platform_profiles`.

field.description: Dot-path prefix the price applies to.

credits.description: Credits per result, for this account.

FilterCondition.description:
One filter leaf. `field` and the operators are exactly those of the dataset's own search
endpoint, so the Person, Company, and Job search references are the full catalog.

field.description:
Dot-path of the field to filter on, for example
`experience.employment_details.current.title` for a person or `job_details.title` for a
job. Field names are unique across datasets, so a leaf naming another dataset's field is
a valid cross-dataset condition rather than a mistake.

type.description:
The comparison operator. Crustdata writes greater-or-equal as `=>` and less-or-equal as
`=<`, not `>=` / `<=`. `not_contains` is an alias of `(!)`.

A cross-dataset leaf may not use a row-level negation operator (`!=`, `not_in`, `(!)`,
`not_contains`, `geo_exclude`): it would match subjects with some *other* matching row
rather than subjects with none. List the values you do want instead.

value.description:
The value to compare against. A scalar for `=`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `=>`, `=<`, and the
substring operators; an array for `in` and `not_in`; an object for the geo operators.
Required for every operator except the null checks.

FilterConditionGroup.description: A group that combines conditions with AND or OR. Groups nest, so an `and` group can sit inside an `or` group's `conditions`.

conditions.description: The conditions to combine. Each item is a leaf or another group.

IdentifyMatch.description: A single company match from /company/identify with confidence score and core company data.

IdentifyResult.description: One result entry in the identify response — one per submitted identifier.

Job.description: Complete job listing with the hiring company's firmographics, job location, description, and metadata.

job_details.description: Core information about the job posting itself.

category.description: High-level job category (e.g., Engineering, Sales, Operations, Consultancy, Others).

workplace_type.description: Workplace type if provided (e.g., Remote, Hybrid, On-site). May be empty.

url.description: Canonical URL for the job posting.

reposted_job.description: Whether the posting was detected as a repost of a prior listing.

number_of_openings.description: Number of openings the posting is hiring for.

company.description: Hiring company's firmographics at the time of indexing.

primary_domain.description: Primary web domain for the company.

professional_network_id.description: Identifier for the company on the professional network profile source.

industries.description: Industry classifications assigned to the company.

locations.description: Company's registered or primary office location.

country.description:
Full country name for the primary office. Filter with the name or an
ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, such as `USA`. Both forms return the same jobs.

state.description: State or region for the primary office.

street_address.description: Full street address for the primary office.
street_address.example: 354 Oyster Point Blvd, South San Francisco, California, United States

headcount.description: Company headcount at the time of indexing.

total.description: Total current headcount across all offices.

largest_headcount_country.description: ISO country code where the company has the most employees.

count.description: Total followers of the company's public profile.

revenue.description: Estimated revenue and public market signals.

estimated.description: Estimated annual revenue range in USD.

lower_bound_usd.description: Lower bound of the estimated annual revenue range, in USD.

upper_bound_usd.description: Upper bound of the estimated annual revenue range, in USD.

public_markets.description: Public market information when the company is listed.

stock_symbols.description: Stock ticker symbols associated with the company.

acquisition_status.description: Acquisition status if known (e.g., acquired, merged).

total_investment_usd.description: Total capital raised to date, in USD.

last_fundraise_date.description: Date of the most recent funding event (ISO 8601).

last_round_type.description: Type of the most recent funding round (e.g., seed, series_a, series_b, secondary_market).

num_funding_rounds.description: Total number of funding rounds recorded.

location.description:
Job's advertised location. The `city`, `state`, and `country` fields are derived
by geocoding the raw location string, so their values are normalized place names
(e.g. `United States` rather than the raw text's country wording).

raw.description: Raw location string as advertised on the job posting.

city.description: City from geocoding the raw location. Empty string when the raw location resolves to a broader area than a city (e.g. a metro area).

district.description: District or borough from geocoding, when the location resolves to that granularity.

state.description: State or province from geocoding the raw location.

country.description: Normalized country name from geocoding the raw location.

pincode.description: Postal or zip code if available.

content.description: Text content of the job posting.

description.example: Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses...

date_added.description: The job-posted date: when the listing was posted on the source portal, in ISO 8601.

date_updated.description: When the job listing was last refreshed (ISO 8601).

JobAutocompleteRequest.description: Request body for autocompleting the values of a single `/job/search` field.

field.description:
The `/job/search` field whose values to autocomplete. Accepts the same
names used in `/job/search` filters, plus their short aliases.

Common values: `title`, `category`, `company.name`, `company.industries`,
`location.country`, `location.city`, `location.state`.

Full set of supported fields: `category`, `city`,
`company.basic_info.industries`, `company.basic_info.name`,
`company.basic_info.primary_domain`, `company.funding.investors`,
`company.funding.last_round_type`, `company.headcount.largest_country`,
`company.headcount.range`, `company.industries`, `company.locations.city`,
`company.locations.country`, `company.locations.state`, `company.name`,
`company.revenue.acquisition_status`,
`company.revenue.public_markets.fiscal_year_end`,
`company.revenue.public_markets.stock_symbols`, `continent`, `country`,
`country_code`, `district`, `fiscal_year_end`, `job_category`,
`job_details.category`, `job_details.title`, `job_details.workplace_type`,
`job_title`, `location`, `location.city`, `location.country`,
`location.district`, `location.raw`, `location.state`, `locations.city`,
`locations.country`, `locations.district`, `locations.location`,
`locations.state`, `state`, `technographics.technologies.category`,
`technographics.technologies.name`, `technology`, `technology_category`,
`title`, `workplace_type`.

query.description: Partial text to match against the field's values. May be an empty string to return top values.

limit.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return. Must be between 1 and 100.

JobAutocompleteResponse.description: Autocomplete suggestions for the requested field and query.

suggestions.description: Matching values for the requested field, ordered by relevance. Empty when nothing matches.

value.description: A suggested value for the requested field.

JobErrorResponse.description: Standard error response returned by job endpoints for all 4xx and 5xx errors, including authentication failures (`type: unauthorized`).

type.description: Category of the error.

metadata.description: Additional structured context (e.g., list of available fields). Often empty.

JobSearchCondition.description: A single filter condition used to narrow job search results.

field.description:
Field name to filter on. Use the exact dot-path below. Only indexed fields
are filterable.

Job details: `job_details.title`, `job_details.category`, `job_details.workplace_type`, `job_details.employment_type`, `job_details.reposted_job`, `job_details.url`

Company basic info: `company.basic_info.company_id`, `company.basic_info.name`, `company.basic_info.primary_domain`, `company.basic_info.professional_network_id`, `company.basic_info.industries`

Company firmographics: `company.headcount.total`, `company.headcount.range`, `company.followers.count`, `company.revenue.estimated.lower_bound_usd`

Location: `location.raw`, `location.country`, `location.state`, `location.district`, `location.city`. For radius filtering with `geo_distance`/`geo_exclude` or polygon filtering with `geo_polygon`, use `location` or `location.raw`, which target the same geo point.

Technographics (filter-only, posting-scoped, never returned in responses): `technographics.technologies.name`, `technographics.technologies.category`, `technographics.technologies.super_category`. A job matches only a technology detected in that exact posting, never one inferred from the hiring company. Two AND conditions on `technographics.technologies.name` match a posting naming both technologies. Values are case-sensitive; discover them with `/job/search/autocomplete`. Only listings with `job_details.source` = `professional_network` carry technographics.

Content: `content.description`

Identifiers: `crustdata_job_id`

Metadata: `metadata.date_added`, `metadata.date_updated`

type.description:
Filter operator.
- `=`, `!=`: exact match or negation
- `<`, `=<`, `>`, `=>`: numeric or date comparison
- `in`, `not_in`: set membership (value must be an array)
- `is_null`, `is_not_null`: field is null/missing, or has a non-null value (value must be a literal null; the `value` key is required)
- `(.)`: case-insensitive substring match (useful for keywords in title or description)
- `[.]`: case-insensitive exact word/phrase match
- `geo_distance`: match jobs within a radius of a point (value must be a geo object; only on `location` and `location.raw`)
- `geo_exclude`: exclude jobs within a radius of a point (value must be a geo object; only on `location` and `location.raw`)
- `geo_polygon`: match jobs located inside a polygon (value must be a polygon object with `points`; only on `location` and `location.raw`)

value.description: Filter value. Type depends on `type`: a scalar for comparison operators, an array for `in`/`not_in`, a literal null for `is_null`/`is_not_null` (the `value` key is still required), a geo object for `geo_distance`/`geo_exclude`, or a polygon object for `geo_polygon`. `job_details.employment_type` takes one of `full_time`, `part_time`, `contract`, `temporary`, `intern`, `volunteer`.

anyOf.description:
Geo radius value for `geo_distance`/`geo_exclude`. Provide a center point as
either a `location` string (geocoded server-side) or an explicit `lat_lng`
pair, plus a `distance` radius. If both `location` and `lat_lng` are supplied,
`lat_lng` is used and geocoding is skipped.

location.description: Free-form place name to geocode into the center point (e.g. a city). Required unless `lat_lng` is provided.

lat_lng.description: Explicit center point as a `[latitude, longitude]` pair of numbers (latitude -90 to 90, longitude -180 to 180). Takes precedence over `location`.

items.description: Latitude or longitude in decimal degrees.

distance.description: Radius around the center point. Must be a positive number, in the unit given by `unit`.

anyOf.description:
Polygon value for `geo_polygon`. The polygon closes itself, so repeating the
first point is optional. Edges may not cross, and no point may be revisited.
Points are coordinates, not place names, and are not geocoded. A polygon that
crosses the 180° meridian must list its points counter-clockwise, or it is
read as everything outside it. A malformed polygon returns `400`.

points.description: Polygon corners as `[latitude, longitude]` pairs (latitude -90 to 90, longitude -180 to 180). At least 3 distinct points and at most 1,000.

items.description: One `[latitude, longitude]` pair in decimal degrees.

JobSearchConditionGroup.description: A group of filter conditions combined with AND or OR logic. Supports nesting for complex queries.

op.description: Logical operator to combine the child conditions.

conditions.description: Array of conditions or nested condition groups.

oneOf.description: Nested filter group (recursive AND/OR of conditions or further groups).

op.description: Logical operator to combine the child conditions.

conditions.description: Array of conditions or further nested groups.

items.description: A filter condition or a further nested filter group.

JobSearchRequest.description: Request body for searching the indexed job dataset with filters, pagination, sorting, field selection, and aggregations.

filters.description:
Search filter conditions. Can be a single condition or a nested group
combined with AND/OR logic. Only indexed fields are filterable — see
`SearchCondition.field` for the full list.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned in a prior response's `next_cursor` field. Pass this to fetch the next page of results with the same filter, sort, and field selection.

limit.description: Maximum number of job listings to return per page. Set to 0 when you only want aggregations.

sorts.description: Sort specifications for ordering results. Sorts are applied in order.

fields.description:
Fields to return in each job listing. Use dot-notation for nested fields
(e.g., "job_details.title", "company.basic_info.name"). If omitted, all
available fields are returned.

Valid top-level groups: `crustdata_job_id`, `job_details`, `company`,
`location`, `content`, `metadata`. Nested fields are supported
(e.g., `company.basic_info`, `company.headcount`, `company.funding`).

aggregations.description: Aggregation queries to run alongside the search. Set `limit: 0` if you want only aggregation results and no job rows.

JobSearchResponse.description: Paginated response from the indexed job search endpoint.

job_listings.description: Job listings matching the search criteria for the current page. Empty when `limit` is 0 or when an aggregation-only query is made.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for fetching the next page of results. Pass this value as `cursor` in the next request. `null` when there are no more pages.

total_count.description: Total number of job listings matching the query across all pages.

aggregations.description: Aggregation results, present only when the request included an `aggregations` array.

JobSearchSort.description: Sort specification for ordering job search results.

field.description:
Field name to sort on. Supports the same dot-path names used for filters,
e.g., `metadata.date_added`, `metadata.date_updated`, `company.headcount.total`,
`company.followers.count`.

ModePrice.description: What one request flag costs this account.

mode.description: Name of the request flag, as sent in the request body.

credits.description:
Credits for this account when the flag is set. On `preview` this
replaces the per-result charge; on `verified` it adds to it.

NotificationChannel.description: One delivery channel. Every channel on a watch receives every notification.

NotificationEnvelope.description:
The body POSTed to each webhook channel, and the same body a test send returns under `envelope`.

The two watch kinds shape `results` differently. A discovery watch keys results by membership
polarity, so records arrive under `results.added`, each one the raw dataset record. An entity
watch delivers a flat list, one object per fired subject, each with its own `changes` and
`record`.

A watch whose `config.payload_delivery_type` is `link` omits `results` entirely and carries the
records' location in `metadata.payload_delivery` instead. Branch on
`metadata.payload_delivery.type` rather than on the presence of `results`: the field is present
on every delivery, and a `link` watch falls back to an inline body when the file cannot be
written.

notification_id.description: Unique id for this delivery, echoed in the `x-crustdata-event-id` header. Key your receiver's deduplication on it.

test.description: Present and `true` only on a test send. Absent on a real delivery.

summary.description:
The run's counts. `records_matched` ships only on an entity watch and `records_stale` only
on a discovery watch, so read `metadata.kind` before you read either one. A key that does
not apply to the watch kind is left out rather than sent as `null`.

total_count.description:
New records the run found, before the cap. On a discovery watch, the new matches.
On an entity watch, the entities that changed, and on its first run every subject
Crustdata resolved. It exceeds `delivered` when the cap cut the run short.

records_searched.description:
What the run started from. On a discovery watch, everything the query returned
before the new-record check and the cap. On an entity watch, the identifiers you
listed in `entities`.

records_matched.description:
Entity watches only. Identifiers that resolved to a record Crustdata holds. A gap
between this and `records_searched` is the part of your list that matches nothing,
which a run would otherwise pass over in silence. Left out on a discovery watch.

records_stale.description:
Discovery watches only. Matches an earlier run already handled, so
`records_searched` minus `records_stale` is `total_count`. On a job or post watch
it counts the records posted before the last run. Left out on an entity watch.

chunk.description:
Present only when an inline run was too large for one request and was split.
Each request then carries its own `notification_id` of `ntf_{run_id}_{index}`.
Absent on a single-request run and on every `link` delivery.

index.description: Zero-based position of this request in the run's sequence.

results.description:
The payload. An object keyed by polarity for a discovery watch, a flat array for an
entity watch. Absent entirely when `metadata.payload_delivery.type` is `link`.

PayloadDelivery.description:
Where the records of this delivery actually travelled. Present on every notification and on
every run summary, so read `type` before reaching for `url`.

An `inline` delivery carries `{"type": "inline"}` and nothing else, and its records sit in the
body under `results`. A `link` delivery carries the whole block and no records: fetch `url`
with a plain `GET` and no `authorization` header, since the pre-signed S3 URL carries its own
authentication in the query string.

The file is NDJSON, one complete JSON object per line with no wrapping array, so you can stream
it without holding the run in memory. Each line is the record the inline body would have
carried: the raw dataset record for a discovery watch, without the `added` wrapper, and the
same `{changes, record}` object for an entity watch.

A watch set to `link` still reports `inline` here when the file could not be written. The
delivery then carries its records in the body as usual, so an outage costs the link and not the
notification.

type.description: Where the records of this delivery travelled.

url.description:
Pre-signed S3 URL for the run's file. Present only when `type` is `link`. Fetch it when
the notification arrives rather than storing it: the signature stops working at
`expires_at`.

format.description: Format of the linked file. Present only when `type` is `link`.

bytes.description: Size of the linked file. Present only when `type` is `link`.

expires_at.description:
When `url` stops working, five days after it was issued. Present only when `type` is
`link`. Reading the run again from the run-summary endpoint issues a fresh link over
the same records.

verdict.description: Authenticity label for the profile. `cannot_verify` means thin evidence rather than fraud, and `probably_fabricated` is a review flag, not a trigger for automated action.

tier.description: Authenticity tier, 0 (most trusted) to 9 (least trusted). Sortable on /person/search, where ascending puts the most trusted first.

PersonAssessment.description: Computed profile assessment. Returned only by /person/enrich, never by default, and not a billed add-on. `verdict` and `tier` are populated independently, so a profile may carry a tier with a null verdict. type.description: Filter operator. Use '=' for exact match, '!=' for not equal, '<' and '>' for exclusive numeric/date comparisons, '=<' for less-than-or-equal, '=>' for greater-than-or-equal, 'in'/'not_in' for set membership (value must be an array), 'is_null'/'is_not_null' for null checks (value must be a literal null and the `value` key is required; on nested-array fields, 'is_null' matches profiles where no element carries the field and 'is_not_null' matches profiles where at least one element has a non-null value), 'has_all' for cross-element matching on a nested-array field (value must be a non-empty array; each listed value must be matched by some array element, possibly different elements — shorthand for an `all_of` group of one equality condition per value), '(.)' for case-insensitive all-words match (every query word must appear, in any order; a piped value is split into separate words that must ALL match (AND), not OR; on some fields it also matches close misspellings, so use '=' or 'in' for known values and '[.]' for exact words), '(!)' for case-insensitive fuzzy negation (excludes substring matches of `value`), '[.]' for case-insensitive exact-phrase match (words must be contiguous and in order), 'geo_distance' for geographic radius inclusion, and 'geo_exclude' for geographic radius exclusion ('geo_distance' keeps profiles inside the radius, 'geo_exclude' removes them; both take an object with `location` or `lat_lng`, plus `distance` and optional `unit`). Use '=<' and '=>' instead of '<=' and '>='. For cross-element logic beyond a single value list, use an `all_of` group (see PersonSearchConditionGroup). On free-text fields such as basic_profile.summary, '=', '!=', 'in' and 'not_in' match a phrase, not the whole value, and 'in' and 'not_in' take at most 1,000 values.

value.description: Filter value. Type depends on operator: For '=', '!=', '<', '>', '=<', '=>': string or number. For 'in', 'not_in': array of strings or numbers. For 'is_null', 'is_not_null': a literal null — the `value` key is still required. For 'has_all': non-empty array of strings or numbers (nested-array fields only). For '(.)': string. A '|' in the value is a word separator, not OR: "VP|Director" matches the same profiles as "VP Director". To match any one of several values, put one '(.)' condition for each value in an `or` group. For '(!)': string; rows whose value contains this substring (case-insensitive) are excluded. Unlike '(.)' / '[.]', multi-word values are matched as a literal phrase (not word-split): `(!) "New York"` excludes only rows that literally contain "New York", not "New Yorker"; send separate `(!)` conditions inside an `and` group to exclude on each word independently. For '[.]': string substring to match. For 'geo_distance'/'geo_exclude': object with one of {location: string} or {lat_lng: [lat, lng]}, plus {distance: number, unit: "km"|"mi"|"miles"|"m"|"ft"}. When both `location` and `lat_lng` are supplied, `lat_lng` is used and geocoding is skipped.

oneOf.description: Object value used by `geo_distance` and `geo_exclude`. Supply either `location` (geocoded server-side) or `lat_lng` (explicit `[lat, lng]`; bypasses geocoding). If both are provided, `lat_lng` wins.

location.description: Reference location (e.g., "San Francisco, CA"). Ignored when `lat_lng` is also provided.

lat_lng.description: Explicit coordinates as `[lat, lng]`. Latitude must be between -90 and 90; longitude must be between -180 and 180. When provided, geocoding is skipped.

A condition inside 'all_of' may itself be an 'and'/'or' group, which is then matched within a single element. The operator is case-sensitive: send exactly 'all_of'.

RealtimeConditionCompany.description:
One `realtime_filters` leaf on a `company` watch (`POST /watch/company/search`). Operators
and values per field:

- `locations.headquarters`: `=` `!=` `in` `not_in`. A headquarters string from
  `POST /company/search/autocomplete`, for example `San Francisco, California, United States`.
  The watch resolves it to the live search's place; a value it cannot resolve is a `400`
  (a preview answers `can_create: false`) asking for another autocomplete value or
  `locations.country`. A tree naming both `locations.headquarters` and an included
  `locations.country` is refused: put the country in `narrowing_filters.company`. An
  excluded country (`!=`, `not_in`) beside it is fine.
- `locations.country`, `taxonomy.professional_network_industry`: `=` `!=` `in` `not_in`. A
  country name, an industry name.
- `basic_info.employee_count_range`: `=` `in`. One of `myself only`, `2-10`, `11-50`, `51-200`,
  `201-500`, `501-1000`, `1001-5000`, `5001-10000`, `10001+`.
- `basic_info.fortune_rank`: `=` `in`. One of `50`, `51-100`, `101-250`, `251-500`.
  Realtime only; the index has no such field.
- `headcount.total`: `=>` `=<`. A bucket edge: `=>` one of `1`, `11`, `51`, `201`, `501`,
  `1001`, `5001`, `10001`; `=<` one of `10`, `50`, `200`, `500`, `1000`, `5000`, `10000`.
- `followers.count`: `=>` `=<`. A bucket edge: `=>` one of `1`, `51`, `101`, `1001`,
  `5001`; `=<` one of `50`, `100`, `1000`, `5000`.
- `headcount.growth_percent.12m`: `=>` `=<`. A percentage.
- `roles.distribution.<department>`: `=>` `=<`. A headcount in that department.
- `roles.growth_yoy.<department>`: `=>` `=<`. A percentage over a fixed 12-month window.
- `revenue.estimated.lower_bound_usd`: `=>` only. USD.
- `revenue.estimated.upper_bound_usd`: `=<` only. USD.
- `technographics.technologies.name`: `=` `in`. A technology name.
- `people.senior_leadership_changed_recently`: `=`. `true` only, covering the last three
  months. Realtime only.
- `funding.*`: any funding field of the company index, with its index operators.
  `funding.last_round_type` takes one of `pre_seed`, `seed`, `angel`, `series_a` to
  `series_j`, `series_unknown`, `private_equity`, `debt_financing`, `convertible_note`,
  `grant`, `corporate_round`, `equity_crowdfunding`, `product_crowdfunding`,
  `secondary_market`, `post_ipo_equity`, `post_ipo_debt`, `post_ipo_secondary`,
  `non_equity_assistance`, `initial_coin_offering`, `undisclosed`. For
  example `funding.last_round_type` `in` `["seed", "series_a"]`, or
  `funding.last_fundraise_date` `=>` / `=<` with an ISO date or date math such as
  `now-30d`. No date window is added for you: add one yourself, or a broad watch is
  refused by the realtime size limit.

A tree naming any `funding.*` field is answered by the company index as written, in any
group shape, and takes `funding.*` fields only. Every other field above is refused in such
a tree. Put a company condition such as location or size in `narrowing_filters.company`
instead. `basic_info.fortune_rank` and `people.senior_leadership_changed_recently` have no
index field, so `narrowing_filters.company` refuses them too. To filter on either one, leave
the `funding.*` fields out: without them, both work as realtime filters beside the other
fields above.

RealtimeConditionGroup.description:
The shape of a `realtime_filters` tree. The live search is an AND of filters, with OR only
between values of one filter, so the tree is either one bare leaf or:

- A top-level `and` group of leaves.
- Inside it, an `or` group only when every leaf names the **same field** with an include
  operator (`=`, `in`, `(.)`). It works as a value list.
- No nested `and` groups.
- No `sorts` on a realtime watch. A live search has no stable order.

Keyword fields (person `basic_profile.headline` and `basic_profile.summary`, job
`job_details.title` and `content.description`, post `text`) feed the live search's one
free-text keyword. Several of them, in `and` or `or` groups, fold into one boolean
expression.

A `company` tree that names any `funding.*` field is the exception. The company index
answers that whole tree as written, so it takes the full index grammar: nested `and` and
`or` groups and every index operator. It names `funding.*` fields only. Put any other
company condition, such as location or size, in `narrowing_filters.company`. A tree that
mixes them is refused. `basic_info.fortune_rank` and
`people.senior_leadership_changed_recently` exist only in the live search, so a funding
watch cannot filter on them. Leave the `funding.*` fields out to use either one.

One `realtime_filters` leaf on a `job` watch (`POST /watch/job/search`). Operators and
values per field:

- `job_details.title`, `content.description`: `=` `(.)`. Free text, the watch's keyword.
  `=` matches exactly, `(.)` loosely. A multi-word value is quoted for you.
- `job_details.workplace_type`: `=` `in`. `On-site`, `Remote`, or `Hybrid`. Any other
  value is refused with `400`, and the message lists these three.
- `job_details.employment_type`: `=` `in`. `full_time`, `part_time`, `contract`,
  `temporary`, `intern`, `volunteer`, or `other`. Any other value is refused with `400`.
- `location.country`, `location.state`, `location.city`: `=` `in`. A bare city or state is
  enough; a country or state beside it places the name more precisely. A place the watch
  cannot resolve is refused with `400`; try another value from Job Autocomplete, or add
  the country.
- `company.basic_info.industries`: `=` `in`. An industry name.
- `company.basic_info.name`: `=` `in`. An employer name, resolved against the company
  index. Every company of that name is followed. A name the index does not hold is
  refused with `400`, and one condition may name at most 300 companies.
- `company.basic_info.professional_network_id`: `=` `in`. The employer's professional
  network id, as a string. Sent as given, with no lookup.

  company IDs before the search runs.
- `experience.employment_details.last_company.name`: `=` `!=` `in` `not_in`. Checked on
  each person the search returns, not sent to the search.
- `experience.employment_details.current.company_headcount_range`: `=` `in`. A headcount

- `experience.employment_details.current.company_industries`,

  `not_in`. An industry name, a country name.

  `basic_profile.location.city`: `=` `!=` `in` `not_in`. A bare city or state is enough: the

  name more precisely, and the watch searches on the most specific one. A place it cannot
  resolve is refused with `400`; try another value from Person Autocomplete, or add the
  country.

- `basic_profile.first_name`, `basic_profile.last_name`: `=`. Free text.
- `education.schools.school`: `=` `!=` `in` `not_in` `(.)`. A school name.

TrackCondition.description:
One `track` leaf: the change on one field that fires a notification. The operator must match the
field's shape, so `changed` needs a scalar path and `added` needs an array path. Mixing them
returns `400`. An `added` leaf may carry `keys` to say which fields identify an element of the
array.

field.description:
Dot-path into the record, addressing the same structure the dataset's enrich endpoint
returns: the fields of `POST /person/enrich` or `POST /company/enrich` are the fields a
watch can track, and there is no separate list. An array path takes `added`; a field
inside an array's items, or any single value, takes `changed`, `increased`/`decreased`
or a comparison. A field that identifies an array item cannot take `changed`, since a
new value there is a new item, and arrays can be tracked at most two levels deep.

type.description:
`changed` fires when a scalar becomes different from the last snapshot. `added` fires
when a new element appears in an array. `increased` and `decreased` fire when a number
moves up or down from the last snapshot, for example `headcount.total` growing; they take
no `value` and are refused on a field that is not a number. The comparison operators fire
when the comparison flips from false to true, for example `professional_network.connections`
crossing 500.

keys.description:
Which fields identify an element of the array, in place of the identity the dataset gives
it. Valid only with `added`: on any other operator the create returns `400` with
`track: 'keys' is only valid with 'added', not '<type>'`. A string entry is one field; a
nested entry is a composite of several fields. Entries are matched as a union, so an
element is already known when any one entry matches, and the loosest entry therefore
wins: give a fallback entry the same fields as the entry it backs up. An entry cannot
identify an element when any field in that entry is null. The fields must belong to the
array's own elements and your key must be entitled to each one, so `keys` on an array of
plain strings returns `400`. A watch remembers every identity it has seen on the array,
so an element that leaves and returns does not fire again. An empty list or a bare
string returns `400` with
`track: '<path>': 'keys' must be a non-empty list of fields or field groups`.

value.description: The threshold to compare against. Required for the comparison operators, omitted for `changed`, `added`, `increased` and `decreased`.

TrackConditionGroup.description:
A group of track conditions. An `or` group fires if any child fires. An `and` group fires only
when all conditions hold and at least one just became true. Groups nest.

WatcherErrorResponse.description:
Every watcher failure, whatever the status code. `type` is the machine-readable code,
`message` is the sentence you can show a user, and `metadata` carries per-problem detail.

Validation collects every failure in one pass, so a body with three problems answers once
with three `metadata` entries and a `message` that joins them. Each validation entry is a
`{field, type, message}` triple: `field` is the request path that failed, indexed into
filter and track trees; `type` is drawn from the vocabulary the search and enrich APIs use
(`missing`, `enum`, `greater_than_equal`, `less_than_equal`, `string_type`, `int_type`,
`bool_type`, `list_type`, `dict_type`, `too_long`, `date_parsing`, `extra_forbidden`,
`invalid`) plus `unknown_field` and `unsupported`, which only watcher emits.

A limit that names no request field, such as the tracking cap, carries an empty `metadata`.
Three responses put something other than a triple in it: `Invalid fields: ...` carries
`available_fields`, `Access denied to fields: ...` carries `denied_fields` and
`permitted_fields`, and a test send that was never attempted carries the `delivered` and
`envelope` it had built. Check for the keys you expect before iterating.
